entries: V Rising — how the game works

New to V Rising? This is a plain-language guide to the base game — what blood, gear level, V Bloods and castles actually do — followed by a summary of how the server mods Raphael supports change the experience. Raphael itself is a UI mod: it does not change the game, it just gives you a nicer interface for it and the mods.

Heads-up: Stunlock patch the game over time and most servers tweak their settings, so treat the numbers below as defaults/typical values. When something seems off for your server, ask your admin or check the official wiki on the Game Guide tab.
Blood, sunlight, and staying alive

You are a vampire. Two things matter from minute one: blood keeps you powered, and the sun kills you. Daylight burns you fast in the open — travel in shade, under cover, or via the world's shadow paths, and build a roof over your base early. Garlic exposure, holy ground, and silver all hurt vampires too (see The world, below).
Details — Blood types & quality

Feeding on a creature gives you its BLOOD TYPE — Warrior, Rogue, Brute, Scholar, Worker, Creature, Draculin, Mutant, Corruption and more — each granting a different set of combat bonuses while you carry it.

Blood has a QUALITY percentage (0–100%). Higher quality = stronger bonuses, and at high quality you unlock extra bonus tiers for that blood type. Feeding from a higher-quality victim raises your blood; taking hits and time lower it.
Your BLOOD POOL is also your resource bar for some abilities and your sustain — it drains in sunlight and over time, so keep topped up by feeding.

Match your blood type to your playstyle: e.g. Warrior for melee damage, Rogue for crit/move speed, Brute for sustain, Scholar for spell power. The right blood at high quality is a real power spike, separate from your gear.
With the mods — Blood

BLOODCRAFT adds Blood Legacies: each blood type levels up the more you use it, granting permanent stat bonuses on top of vanilla blood bonuses, plus prestige on each legacy. See the Blood Legacy tab and the Bloodcraft Guide for the full breakdown.
Gear Level is your "level"

Vanilla V Rising has NO experience bar or character levels. Your power is your GEAR LEVEL — a single number computed from the tier of your equipped weapon, armor, and the spells/jewels you have slotted. Better gear = higher gear level = you hit harder and take less from same-level enemies.

Every enemy and boss has a level too. Fighting something far above your gear level means your hits are heavily reduced and theirs are amplified — so the loop is: beat content near your level, craft the better gear it unlocks, raise your gear level, move to the next tier.
Details — Weapons, spells & vampire powers

WEAPONS: each weapon type (mace, sword, spear, crossbow, slashers, greatsword, pistols, longbow, twinblades, whip, axes, …) has its own feel plus two special attacks. Swapping weapons to suit the fight is normal play.
SPELLS come in schools — Blood, Unholy, Chaos, Frost, Illusion, Storm. You slot abilities into your spell slots and an ultimate; JEWELS modify and upgrade individual spells.
VAMPIRE POWERS: dodge/travel abilities, the bat form for fast travel (unlocked later), and utility powers all come from progression.
Most new abilities, spells, and recipes are unlocked by defeating V Blood bosses (next section) — that's the spine of vanilla progression.
With the mods — Combat & progression

BLOODCRAFT bolts a full RPG layer onto vanilla's gear-only power: character XP and levels, Classes, Weapon Expertise (weapons level with use and grant stats), and Prestige. Your effective power becomes gear + level + expertise + legacy + class, not just gear. See the Class, Weapon (Expertise), Levels and Prestige tabs, and the Bloodcraft Guide.
BEELZEBUB lets you capture enemy abilities and equip them in custom loadouts, and unlocks transform forms (Dracula / Morgana). See the Beelzebub Guide.
V Bloods: the backbone of progress

V Bloods are special named bosses scattered across the world, each at a set level. Defeating one lets you consume its powerful blood, which permanently UNLOCKS rewards: new spells, weapon abilities, crafting recipes, structures, and travel powers. You hunt them roughly in level order.

Use the in-game Blood Altar to track and locate the next V Bloods available to you — it's your to-do list for the whole game. Clearing V Bloods is what raises your crafting options and, with it, your gear level.
Details — Crafting, refinement & servants

RESOURCES flow through refinement chains: raw materials → refined goods (planks, ingots, scrolls, etc.) at the right station → crafted gear/structures. Higher tiers need stations and recipes unlocked from V Bloods.
SERVANTS: later you can convert defeated humans into castle servants, sending them on expeditions for loot/resources. Servant power scales with the blood you converted them with.
HORSES can be tamed for fast overland travel; the bat form (late unlock) gives flight between discovered points.
Inventory/crafting management is a big time sink in vanilla — which is exactly what some mods streamline (see below).
With the mods — Progression & logistics

BLOODCRAFT adds Familiars (defeated enemies can become summonable combat companions, stored in boxes), Professions (gathering/crafting skills that level up), and Daily Quests. See the Familiars / Boxes / All Familiars / Daily Quest tabs and the Bloodcraft Guide.
KINDREDLOGISTICS automates inventory: auto-stashing, pulling from network storage, and sorting — removing much of the manual hauling. See the Kindred Logistics tab.
URIEL adds shared storage between players, public prisons, live stair restyling, and spawning decorative/utility objects, plus Castle Events (defend your castle against waves). See the Uriel Guide.
Castle Heart, territory & upkeep

Your base is built around a CASTLE HEART placed on a territory plot. The Heart claims the surrounding territory, powers your crafting stations and defenses, and must be FUELED with blood essence (gathered from kills / greater blood essence). Let it run dry and your castle enters DECAY — structures degrade and eventually can be lost.
Upgrading the Heart raises your castle level, which increases your servant cap and territory size. Plots are limited, so good early spots get claimed fast on busy servers.
Details — Raiding, decay & offline protection

On PvP servers, castles can be raided during set windows; on PvE servers they can't. Which applies, the raid windows, decay rates, and offline-protection rules are all SERVER SETTINGS — ask your admin or check the server's rules.
Keep the Heart fueled and your blood-essence stock up, especially before logging off, so you don't return to a decaying castle.
Territory and plot availability change as players come and go — a freed plot becomes claimable.
With the mods — Castles & server info

FAUST is an information/investigation mod: it surfaces castle ownership, plot size/availability, decay timers, player playtime, V Blood boss status, leaderboards, and a world map — extremely handy for finding open plots or planning. See the Faust Guide tab.
KINDREDCOMMANDS gives admins the command tools to manage players, castles, and the server.
Map, travel & vampire weaknesses

The world is divided into regions that rise in danger and level as you go outward. Discover WAYGATES to fast-travel between them (you can't carry most resources through waygates by default). World bosses, resource nodes, and points of interest dot each region.

Vampire hazards to respect: SUNLIGHT burns you in the open during the day; GARLIC exposure stacks a debuff indoors in human settlements; HOLY ground and holy enemies deal bonus damage; and SILVER (including silver coins in your inventory) burns you until you have silver resistance. Resistances are improved through gear, consumables, and progression.
Details — Difficulty & PvP vs PvE
Servers run at different difficulties (e.g. relaxed → standard → brutal), which scale enemy strength and your durability.
PvE servers focus on co-op/solo progression with no castle raiding or player-vs-player combat; PvP servers add player combat and (windowed) raiding. The exact ruleset is server-defined.
Clan size, drop rates, blood quality, and many other knobs vary per server — your experience can differ a lot from another server's.
What each server mod adds

Raphael is a unified UI for several server-side mods. WHICH of these you actually have depends on your server — Raphael auto-detects them and shows the matching tab groups. Here's the short version of what each one does; open its guide in Settings and Help for everything else.
Bloodcraft — RPG progression

Turns gear-only vanilla into a full RPG: character XP & levels, Classes, Weapon Expertise, Blood Legacies, Prestige (incl. endgame Exo prestige + Exoform shapeshifts), Familiars, Professions, and Daily Quests. The biggest gameplay change of the set. → Bloodcraft Guide.
Beelzebub — abilities & transforms
Capture abilities from enemies and slot them into custom loadouts (universal + per-weapon), bind extra abilities to hotkeys, and unlock transform forms (Dracula / Morgana). → Beelzebub Guide.
Uriel — sharing, prisons & building

Share storage chests with other players (with permissions/limits), run public prisons, restyle stairs live, spawn an unlocked palette of decorative/utility objects, and run Castle Events: waves of enemies that attack a castle, for rewards. → Uriel Guide.
Faust — server information

A read-only intel layer: castle/plot info, decay watch, player playtime & frequency, V Blood boss status, kill/playtime leaderboards, and a filterable world map. Great for finding plots, planning hunts, and admin oversight. → Faust Guide.
Nyarlathotep — world events

Admin-run world events: spawn waves, empowered enemies, bosses that pursue players, regional rules and announcements, started by pillars, timers or triggers. Players see what is running and where. → Nyarlathotep Guide.
Kindred suite — logistics & admin
KindredLogistics automates inventory (auto-stash, network pull, sorting). KindredCommands is an admin/player command toolkit. → Kindred Guide.
Want more detail?

This guide is a primer. For authoritative base-game detail (exact numbers, maps, boss locations) use the official wiki and community links on the Game Guide tab. For each mod's full mechanics and command list, use its guide in this same Settings and Help group. Anything server-specific — drop rates, raid windows, rewards — is best confirmed with your server admin.
